transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-02-11
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~65 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording ID: ff-20260211-sentinel-001

Summary:
Redwood AE + SE team walked through customer's SIG questionnaire high-risk items, discussed SOC 2 / ISO artifacts, RBAC and SSO implementation, audit log retention and KMS/encryption controls. Customer asked about evidence handoff and timeline for a pilot. Action items and a technical deep-dive on encryption were agreed.

Topics covered:
- SIG (standardized information gathering) approach and which sections Redwood can pre-fill
- SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 artifacts availability
- RBAC scopes, SSO (SAML/SCIM) capabilities and provisioning
- Audit logs: retention, access, tamper-evidence
- Encryption at rest and in transit; KMS, HSM, BYOK options and key rotation
- Data residency: multi-region options and EU data controls
- Evidence transfer options (secure SFTP, shared blob with id-based access)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Sofia (Redwood AE): All right thanks everyone for joining, um we'll run through the SIG items that you flagged as high priority. I'm Sofia from Redwood. Diego and Kara are with me, Diego will own the encryption questions.
[00:12] Aisha (CISO) : Hi all, thanks. We have a long questionnaire, we've highlighted SOC two, audit logs and KMS as blockers for legal.
[00:20] Diego (Redwood SE): Great, yeah we prepared answers for the SIG. Quick note - some of the wording in SIG overlaps with CAIQ, so we'll point you to the canonical doc.
[00:30] Tom (Head of IT): Also curious about SSO details - we use Okta and need SCIM provisioning.
[00:37] Sofia: Yep Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. We wire up SSO at the org-level, and we can enable RBAC with directory groups so you get least-privilege.
[00:47] Leo (Security Analyst): How granular is RBAC? Can we restrict who can download audit logs or request service-level metrics?
[00:55] Kara (Redwood SE): You can scope by role and resource, e.g., admin/ops/read-only. We have an audit role that can read logs, and a separate compliance role for evidence export. There's an API with token scopes as well.
[01:10] Aisha: And SAML assertions - do you support attribute mappings for our groups? We have custom group names.
[01:16] Diego: Yes, we map attributes. There was an older doc that said we only accept nameID - that was a prior version, we've since added group/attribute mapping and SCIM for provisioning.
[01:25] Tom: Good. On the audit logs, what's retention by default? Our policy is 12 months with 7 years for some records.
[01:33] Sofia: Default retention is 12 months for standard plans, enterprise accounts can extend retention. We can stream logs to your SIEM or to an S3 bucket in your account for long-term retention.
[01:44] Priya (Procurement): If we export logs to our S3, is Redwood able to redact PII before export? That's a legal must for us.
[01:52] Diego: We have pre-export filters and we also offer tenant-level pseudonymization. For full PII removal you'd typically handle it downstream, but we can support a pipeline that masks fields before export. We'll include that in the evidence notes.
[02:08] Aisha: Encryption - we need to see KMS architecture and confirm keys are not stored in plaintext. Also BYOK or customer-managed keys is preferred.
[02:17] Diego: We support both Redwood-managed keys and BYOK with integrations to AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSMs for on-prem HSMs. Keys are never stored in plaintext; we use envelope encryption and the master keys live in KMS/HSM. Key rotation is configurable; default rotation is 90 days, and you can set a rotation policy.
[02:34] Aisha: Do you support HSM-backed key storage for EU-only workloads?
[02:38] Diego: Yes, for Private deployments we can integrate with HSMs in your network or a cloud HSM in the selected region. For Hosted we offer KMS in-region with HSM protections. We'll send a diagram.
[02:48] Sofia: We'll attach a KMS/HSM architecture slide and a short note on rotation and compromise procedures.
[02:54] Tom: SOC 2 - can you provide the latest Type II report and system description? Legal needs the period covered.
[03:00] Sofia: Absolutely - we can share the SOC 2 Type II PDF and the system description. The report covers Jan-Dec 2025. I'll share a link to the secure portal.
[03:10] Leo: Are logs tamper-evident? We need assurance for chain-of-custody.
[03:15] Kara: Logs are signed and stored with immutable retention in our internal store; when we stream to your S3 we can provide verifiable checksums and write-once flags in the bucket policy. We also support forward-integrity signing.
[03:30] Aisha: Data residency - some PHI must stay in the EU. Can you host dedicated instances in eu-west-1?
[03:36] Diego: Yep, Dedicated or Private deployments can be pinned to a region. For Hosted API we have EU tenancy options and we can set routing to only serve EU data from EU capacity. We'll document the routing policy and data flows.
[03:48] Tom: How about backups? Are backups encrypted and are they stored in the same region?
[03:52] Kara: Backups are encrypted at rest, encrypted using the same KMS keys by default, and stored in the same region unless you opt into cross-region replication. For EU-only customers we can disable cross-region replication.
[04:02] Priya: Evidence handoff - how do we get artifacts? We prefer an SFTP or secure share to attach to our GRC tool.
[04:08] Sofia: We can do secure SFTP, or provide time-limited links on our portal. For high-sensitivity evidence we also support a one-time secure transfer to your SFTP. We'll include instructions.
[04:18] Aisha: On the SIG spreadsheet itself, which sections can Redwood pre-fill vs which we must answer?
[04:23] Sofia: We'll pre-fill network, encryption, logging, and controls mapping areas. We won't answer vendor-specific legal questions about contract language. We'll mark those as 'customer to confirm'.
[04:34] Tom: Any third-party subprocessors we should be aware of?
[04:37] Diego: We use a few cloud providers, and certain analytics vendors. We'll provide the subprocessors list and their certificates. There's a standard subprocessors PDF.
[04:45] Leo: Regarding incident response, can you provide playbooks and SLA for notification? For example, breach notification within 72 hours?
[04:52] Kara: Our incident response playbook includes detection, containment, and notification. We have contractual breach notification timelines we can include (standard is 72 hours for confirmed breaches). We'll attach the IR playbook summary.
[05:04] Aisha: One more technical, about KV cache and memory - our risk team had a note about persistent caches. Are session caches flushed?
[05:12] Diego: The KV cache is ephemeral per session unless you configure long-lived caches for performance. We can set TTLs and evictions and document the default behavior (no persistent sensitive data). We'll include an explanation and sample config.
[05:26] Speaker 1: (inaudible)
[05:30] Sofia: Quick pause - does anyone have show-stoppers?
[05:33] Priya: Nothing yet, still need to see SOC2 and KMS details.
[05:37] Aisha: Also want the RBAC screenshots - how admins look in the console.
[05:41] Sofia: We'll capture screenshots and redact identifying bits.
[05:45] Diego: For the SIG specific answers on encryption, we'll provide the exact CISQ/CAIQ mapping. Some fields in CAIQ use different phrasing, so we'll call out equivalencies in a mapping sheet.
[05:58] Tom: If we move to a pilot, what's the expected timeline? We have budget decision in early March.
[06:05] Sofia: If you sign the pilot, we can spin up a dedicated test environment in 2-3 weeks. For Private deployment it'll be longer, ~6-8 weeks depending on network setup.
[06:16] Aisha: Procurement question: will you accept our standard security addendum?
[06:21] Sofia: We review SAAs case-by-case; we typically accept many commercial terms but ask for a redline. We'll have legal engage once you send the form.
[06:28] Leo: Any performance or throughput limits for the test env that affect logging or retention?
[06:33] Diego: Test envs default to limited throughput but logs and retention behave the same; if you need production-like load for benchmarking we'll request a short Dedicated trial.
[06:44] Sofia: Okay last part, we'll summarize next steps. We'll send: 1) Draft SIG answers and evidence bundle, 2) SOC 2 Type II PDF link, 3) KMS/HSM architecture diagram and rotation notes, 4) RBAC console screenshots, and 5) subprocessors list.
[06:58] Aisha: Sounds good, appreciate the clarity.
[07:02] Priya: Thanks everyone.
[07:05] Sofia: Thanks all, we'll follow up via email and post links to the secure portal.
